summary:
I developed SpaceHealth, an astronaut health monitoring dashboard designed to help astronauts track their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. The system focuses on six main areas: cardiovascular health, sleep, radiation exposure, bone health, mental wellness, and overall health trends. It brings important health information together in one dashboard using visual graphs, daily reports, and warning notifications.

SpaceHealth addresses the challenge by helping astronauts recognize changes in their health and monitor their condition while living in space. It compares health measurements with each astronaut’s personal baseline to identify unusual changes over time. It also provides suggested next steps, such as repeating a measurement or contacting the medical team when necessary. This is especially important because astronauts experience challenges such as microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and limited access to medical assistance. By organizing health information in one accessible place, SpaceHealth can support better health awareness, early identification of potential problems, and communication with medical professionals. The goal is to make long-duration space missions safer by helping astronauts take a more active role in monitoring their health.
details: SpaceHealth is a health-monitoring software system designed to help astronauts track their physical and mental health during space missions. It works by collecting information from wearable sensors, medical devices, and daily astronaut check-ins. The software organizes this information and displays it on a digital dashboard using graphs, health indicators, and reports. It monitors six main areas: heart health, sleep, radiation exposure, bone health, mental wellness, and overall health trends. The system compares new measurements with each astronaut’s usual health levels to identify unusual changes. If a potential problem is detected, it displays a warning and suggests next steps, such as repeating a measurement or contacting the medical team. The software can store information onboard the spacecraft so astronauts can access their health records even when communication with Earth is limited. Its purpose is to help astronauts understand their health, recognize potential problems early, and make long-duration space missions safer.
